s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers
salient_findings: Sudden-onset chest pain
Tachycardia with a pulse of 120 beats/min
Elevated high-sensitivity troponin I and brain-type natriuretic peptide
ECG findings of ST-segment elevation and PR-segment depression
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
History of hypertension
No history of acute febrile illness
No family history of sudden cardiac death
Normal blood pressure
Elevated white blood cell count
Normal serum calcium
High-sensitivity troponin I: 1.15 ng/mL
Brain-type natriuretic peptide: 1060.30 pg/mL
ECG showed sinus tachycardia and ST-segment elevation
Coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries
Left ventriculography confirmed systolic apical ballooning
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT revealed a left-adrenal heterogeneous mass

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers
salient_findings: Sudden-onset chest pain
Tachycardia with a pulse of 120 beats/min
Elevated high-sensitivity troponin I and brain-type natriuretic peptide
ECG findings of ST-segment elevation and PR-segment depression
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
History of hypertension
No history of acute febrile illness
No family history of sudden cardiac death
Normal blood pressure
Elevated white blood cell count
Normal serum calcium
High-sensitivity troponin I: 1.15 ng/mL
Brain-type natriuretic peptide: 1060.30 pg/mL
ECG showed sinus tachycardia and ST-segment elevation
Coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries
Left ventriculography confirmed systolic apical ballooning
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT revealed a left-adrenal heterogeneous mass

raw.rationale: The presence of a left-adrenal heterogeneous mass on the contrast-enhanced abdominal CT, along with the patient's presentation of sudden-onset chest pain, tachycardia, and hypertension history, points towards pheochromocytoma, a catecholamine-secreting tumor that can cause cardiac and other systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has apical ballooning on left ventriculography, which is characteristic of stress cardiomyopathy, the presence of an adrenal mass suggests an alternative diagnosis that could explain both the cardiac findings and the mass.

rejected.label: Apical ballooning syndrome
rejected.why: Similar to stress cardiomyopathy, apical ballooning syndrome is characterized by the transient ballooning of the left ventricular apex, but it does not account for the adrenal mass found in the patient.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries, which makes acute myocardial infarction due to coronary artery occlusion less likely.

rejected.label: Chagas disease
rejected.why: There is no mention of the patient having a history of exposure to or infection with Trypanosoma cruzi, the parasite that causes Chagas disease, and the presence of an adrenal mass does not correlate with this diagnosis.
